A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSHN research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching the reordered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments on 12 real-world datasets and three synthetic settings, alongside sensitivity and computational-efficiency results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds molecular-reaction hyperedge classification and further computational-cost comparisons.

M1.justification: The core Laplacian, restriction-map learning, and DSHNLight gradient detachment are retained. v2 Appendix D.6 adds a task-specific readout: summing final node representations within each hyperedge through H-transpose times Xnode before classification. This extends the output procedure to hyperedge predictions.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original real-world and synthetic node-classification coverage and adds Molecular-1 and Molecular-2 reaction-type classification. These introduce a new domain and prediction task using native directed hypergraphs whose tails represent reagents and heads represent products, beyond the earlier graph-derived real-world benchmarks.

E2.justification: The original node-classification comparisons retain the same 13 baseline configurations; UniGNNII is corrected to UniGCNII in Table 2. v2 Table 7 newly compares DSHNLight's computational resources with ED-HNN, SheafHyperGNN, and DHGNN, extending the earlier DSHN-versus-DSHNLight resource comparison. These methods already appeared in accuracy comparisons.

E3.justification: The molecular experiments introduce Morgan-fingerprint inputs and F1-score evaluation instead of node-classification accuracy. v2 Appendix C.2 also describes layer normalization as optional and tuned, replacing v1's stated application to W1 and W2. Original node splits and training/search budgets remain unchanged; the revised normalization description does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Table 7 adds a baseline-relative analysis of FLOPs and parameter counts across 12 datasets, examining DSHNLight's resource overhead beyond its comparison with DSHN. The charge sensitivity, depth/stalk-dimension analyses, and matched-parameter accuracy comparison are retained, with the latter moving from Figure 5 to Figure 4.

E5.justification: Both versions report node-classification means and standard deviations over 10 independent runs and retain the 10-run resource-summary practice. The new molecular table uses mean ± standard deviation without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure. No new confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed-reporting practices appear.

E6.justification: v2 adds molecular F1 results and the resource measurements in Table 7. Table 5 reports DSHNLight at 82.32 ± 0.56 versus GeDi-HNN at 80.72 ± 0.78 on Molecular-1, where DSHN is OOM; on Molecular-2, DSHN scores 89.09 ± 3.08 versus AllSetTransformer's 87.89 ± 2.87. Tables 1 and 4 also revise PhenomNN's Squirrel accuracy from 43.62 ± 4.29 to 39.45 ± 2.19. These are added results and a revised baseline score, not same-setting improvements between DSHN versions.

T1.justification: The theorem set is retained, but v2 removes the erroneous outer exponential from Theorem 5's phase definition and corrects the counterexample spectrum in old Appendix D/new Appendix E. Theorem 3's quadratic-form step is revised but remains malformed. Lemma 1 also introduces an inconsistent neighbor normalization, replacing D_v^(-1/2) with D_u^(-1/2). These are local mathematical corrections and regressions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: directed cellular sheaves, a spectrally principled unifying Laplacian, and strong directed-hypergraph performance. The abstract still describes seven real-world datasets, 13 baselines, and 2%–20% relative accuracy gains. The additional experiments support the existing thesis without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds an opinion-dynamics explanation of sheaf representations and stronger interpretations linking spectral properties to stable, localized Fourier convolutions. Appendix C.1 explicitly interprets restriction maps as a source of overhead relative to other models. Appendix B.1 removes the hypothesis that intermediate charge values explain the synthetic advantage; the dense-hyperedge cost limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link and a reproducibility statement directing readers to README setup and execution instructions. It documents molecular data sources, fingerprint features, dataset sizes, label distributions, and the hyperedge readout. Hardware and existing hyperparameter ranges are retained, while the earlier disclosure about adapting DHGNN's approximate Laplacian implementation is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on opinion dynamics, graph signal processing, sheaf recommendation, and molecular data/descriptors, including Hansen and Ghrist, Shuman et al., and Rogers and Hahn. It removes the Jacot et al. citation and the detailed DHMConv-exclusion discussion. The central positioning relative to prior sheaf and directed-hypergraph Laplacians remains.

P1.justification: v2 adds targeted explanatory paragraphs, acknowledgements, and reproducibility, ethics, and LLM-use statements. Implementation details move from Appendix E to C, experimental setup from C to D, and the prior-Laplacian critique from D to E. Author information and terminology receive edits, while the main section sequence and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds molecular-result Table 5, computational-comparison Table 7, and label-distribution Tables 9–10. Existing figures are retained with relocation, renumbering, and limited styling changes; the original dataset-statistics table becomes Table 8. Conference headers, title/author layout, and mathematical typography also change without a wholesale redesign of the existing displays.

improvement.justification: The native molecular-hypergraph experiments add useful applicability evidence beyond v1's graph-derived real-world node benchmarks. Broader resource comparisons and documented code access also improve the paper, and the corrected counterexample strengthens its mathematical presentation. These gains are tempered by v2's misattribution of Molecular-1's 82.32 score to DSHN despite Table 5 assigning it to DSHNLight and marking DSHN OOM, unspecified F1 averaging, and local proof regressions such as Lemma 1's normalization error. The net improvement is therefore limited.
